pr_title: Defer constant loading of `ActiveRecord::DestroyAssociationAsyncJob` via a String instead of a class constant
pr_body:
### Summary

Closes #45434.

- Removes the assignment of `ActiveRecord::DestroyAssociationAsyncJob` from the ActiveJob Railtie.
- Avoids referencing the Job constants until `ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job)` has been triggered.
- ~~Uses nested `ActiveSupport.on_loads` which are ok, according to https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/45434#issuecomment-1164711433~~
- Deprecates `ActiveRecord::ActiveJobRequiredError` and will either raise a `NameError` (if the job class is unloadable) or a `ActiveRecord::ConfigurationError` (if dependent: :destroy_async`  is declared on an association but there is no job class configured)
pr_comments: A better fix would always accept strings in the configuration and only convert to a constant in the first time the value is used, and cache it.

@rafaelfranca Thank you! I changed the implementation to use a String value as you suggested. I wanted to maintain the `class_attribute` behavior of allowing child classes to set a new value without changing the parent's value, but I struggled a bit to keep it compact. Do you know a better class_attribute-memoization strategy than this?

If you're okay with my implementation approach, I could also extract this to a concern to better organize/group the related behavior. And then do the same for #45486.

> I do have objections. We have load hooks exactly to allow us to avoid checking if a component is defined or not. This setting was being set in Active Job exactly to avoid the problem of the application to run without destroy_association_async_job being set because ActiveJob::Base wan't loaded.
>
> I don't think this PR is correct.

Shouldn't both load hooks still be necessary if the initializer was in Active Job? I thought `ActiveJob::Base` shouldn't be defined until after initializers run whether they are defined in Active Record or Active Job railties

Documenting the goals here because I have learned _a ton_ about autoloading and rails boot/initialization through the conversation. Thank you!

- Avoid statically referencing autoloaded abstract classes like `ActiveRecord::Base` or `ActiveJob::Base` (or their children) to avoid autoloading them prematurely during boot or unnecessarily in Development.
- Because `ActiveRecord::Base` and `Activejob::Base` are autoloaded, we can't rely on their `on_load('...')` hooks respectively _ever_ triggering in Development.
- Eagerload (e.g. eager autoload) as many classes as possible in in Production. Application files are eagerloaded (e.g. MyModel, MyJob, etc.) but their parent abstract classes (e.g. `ActiveRecord::Base`) are not eagerloaded. I presume we want to avoid eagerloading those abstract classes if they will not be needed.
- We don't want to create a hard dependency between ActiveRecord and ActiveJob. If ActiveJob isn't present, ActiveRecord shouldn't have broken behavior; and vice-versa.
- Speculative: I think that an application should be able to provide an ActiveJob-compatible _interface_, without ActiveJob being present
- I would like the pattern used here to be applicable to other community gems (which why I didn't like the ActiveRecord configuration living in ActiveJob; community gems can't do that).

I think I can thread all these needles with a few changes :-)
@rafaelfranca @jonathanhefner I think I have addressed all of your comments on this PR and it's ready for re-review.
@jonathanhefner I integrated your deprecation suggestions. That also spurred me to add a changelog entry too. This has been a great experience, I've learned something new with every comment 😅
Thank you @jonathanhefner. I really appreciate the help ❤️  This gives me a lot to think about when it comes to #45486 😄

Thank *you*, @bensheldon!  And thank you for your work on [GoodJob](https://github.com/bensheldon/good_job) (linking for anyone who hasn't seen it)! :heart:

I will take a pass at #45486 tomorrow. :raised_hands:

issue_context.title: Defer constant loading ActiveRecord `destroy_association_async_job` during Rails initialization
issue_context.body:
ActiveRecord's `destroy_association_async_job` currently loads an ActiveJob Job constant during ActiveRecord's initialization. Introduced in #40157

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/4d5a570cfe1890f71a1d198a5fe40d528f2b60d4/activejob/lib/active_job/railtie.rb#L45-L47

That means that loading ActiveRecord triggers loading the Job constant, which triggers initializing ActiveJob, which then triggers initializing the ActiveJob adapter. I have seen this cause an autoloading deadlock if somewhere during this chain an ActiveRecord constant is touched.

A similar autoload chain is also present with [`ActionMailer.delivery_job`](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/1003e974ed9cdae6a057a1857374bceb09b34a7b/actionmailer/lib/action_mailer/railtie.rb#L44-L46) but I have yet to see it deadlock (probably because people are less likely to reference an ActionMailer constant in their ActiveJob configuration).

Aside: I also think that the ActiveJob initializer linked above should be inverted such that it lives in ActiveRecord and is assigned `on_load(:active_job)`; that makes it more consistent with ActionMailers Railtie behavior. I don't think this impacts the autoload behavior though, just an observation.

### Expected behavior

This loading could be deferred if instead of a constant, `destroy_association_async_job` was configured with a string that was then constantized when the behavior is invoked.
comments: Related: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/21acc7bfb6e12f66b6b61a3548e971c64ff7f546/actiontext/lib/action_text/engine.rb#L62-L66 a nested load hook was added to Action Text to tackle a similar issue. However, I'm not sure how safe that is as I think its tying the functionality to load order

@skipkayhil thank you for that! I'm thinking that maybe the problem here is not the _constant_ but is the load order, and the simpler issue is actually what I referred to as an aside:

>  I also think that the ActiveJob initializer linked above should be inverted such that it lives in ActiveRecord and is assigned on_load(:active_job)

Hmm, the inversion could be interesting. I _think_ it still ends up complicated because the configuration is defined on `ActiveRecord::Base`, and we shouldn't be loading that during initialization.

For example:
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/2f5dcb7255e59fdf093fb92b681a737ebab99520/activerecord/lib/active_record/railtie.rb#L76-L78

Even in the Active Record Railtie we need the Active Record load hook

I agree this needs the https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/45434#issuecomment-1163602303 treatment. It's safe: `on_load` will fire immediately if the specified component is already loaded.

I do tend to agree it feels like this line would better live in AR, with the job class etc. /cc @rafaelfranca

> It's safe: `on_load` will fire immediately if the specified component is already loaded.

🙏 thank you for the confirmation, I opened a PR to document this: #45453
